title: Sequential Decision-Value Triage for Task-Specific Paper Reproduction
hook: The cheapest faithful reproduction check is often not the most useful next check: selecting paired probes by expected decision information should lower normalized cost-to-correct adoption without increasing false adoption or false rejection. The procedure stops with adopt, reject, or inconclusive before full reproduction while remaining tied to paper-intervention effects on independently specified user tasks.
hook_shape_rationale: This is a surprising empirical reveal: the named cost-to-correct-adoption metric is predicted to decrease even when the available probes and total budget are held fixed, because their order is chosen by decision information rather than price or fidelity. Counter-intuitive minimalism was also viable, but rejected because the claim is not merely that fewer checks suffice; it is that check order changes which sign decision is reached at a given cost.

gap_closure.gap: Under a limited initial budget, no retrieved frontier establishes that the observed low-fidelity score preserves the sign and ordering of paper interventions by the performance improvement they later produce on independently specified user tasks; a probe can therefore support the wrong go/no-go decision even when it is internally faithful.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by reformulating screening as a posterior measurement of the signed user-task net benefit and greedily selecting the paired probe with the largest expected reduction in adoption decision loss per unit cost.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved paper tests whether tasks derived from the paper or skill, or selected by a fixed reproduction benchmark, are representative enough of the user's target-task distribution to support an adoption decision.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by drawing probes only from preregistered user-task strata and running the paper intervention against a matched no-intervention control on the same task, model, environment, scorer, and seed, so artifact-conditioned task generation cannot inflate utility.

core_mechanism: For a paper intervention P and matched no-intervention control B, define per-task net utility u(P,x) = alpha_h[s_h(P,x)-s_h(B,x)] - sum_r beta_r max(0,s_r(B,x)-s_r(P,x)) - lambda_g g - lambda_a a - lambda_l l, where all task scores s are normalized to [0,1], r indexes preregistered non-headline guardrails, g is GPU-hours, a is API dollars, l is adaptation person-hours, and alpha_h, beta_r, lambda_g, lambda_a, and lambda_l are user-declared conversion weights fixed before probing. The shared object is mu_P = sum_h w_h E[u(P,x) | x in user stratum h], where the user-task strata and weights w_h are fixed from the eight locked real-reuse tasks or a declared target workflow before the paper's probes are inspected; paper- or skill-generated tasks never set these weights. A candidate check q is the smallest executable paper-claim intervention on one user-task stratum, and it always runs P_q and B on the same input, agent model, environment, scorer, and random seed, returning a paired outcome vector o_q plus measured cost c_q = lambda_g g_q + lambda_a a_q + lambda_l l_q. Historical paper-task pairs with full paired endpoints fit a calibrated likelihood for o_q conditioned on paper family, task stratum, agent model, environment, and the sign of mu_P, using leave-one-paper-family-out calibration so the held-out paper cannot train its own decision rule. After observations O_t, the triage state is the posterior over mu_P and the stopping risk R_t = min{L_FA Pr(mu_P <= 0 | O_t), L_FR Pr(mu_P > 0 | O_t), L_I}, with preregistered false-adoption, false-rejection, and inconclusive losses. For every still-unrun check, compute the load-bearing expected decision information value EDIV_t(q) = [R_t - E_{o_q} R_{t+1}(q,o_q)] / c_q and execute the feasible q with maximal positive EDIV_t(q), then update the same posterior from its paired outcome. The preregistered stop is adopt when Pr(mu_P > 0 | O_t) >= 0.95, reject when Pr(mu_P > 0 | O_t) <= 0.05, and inconclusive when the budget is exhausted or max_q EDIV_t(q) <= 0 before either threshold is crossed; thresholds, losses, task weights, and the check catalog are frozen before outcomes are revealed. Evaluation is scoped to leave-one-case-out replay on the locked real-reuse cases and compares each triage decision with the sign from the corresponding full paired reproduction. This is not multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization: it neither optimizes a configuration nor assumes a common resource-fidelity curve, because heterogeneous checks are selected solely for information about the sign of user-distribution net benefit; it is also not an agent workflow or artifact checklist, because a check that does not update calibrated decision risk has no role in the method.
core_mechanism_reasoning: The two selected gaps share one computable object, mu_P: the anchor supplies sequential decision-value selection, while the sibling makes its evidence user-distribution-valid through matched intervention/control tasks; cost and regressions remain terms of the anchor estimand rather than extra paper legs. C00 was chosen over C21 because supervision is not missing and over C27 because no strategic equilibrium is present; C02 supplies the controlled user-task instances needed to make the measurement causal rather than artifact-conditioned. We rejected fixed cheap-to-expensive ladders and generic BOHB/Hyperband allocation because the lineage flags that occupied node and paper checks lack a common fidelity axis; EDIV instead prices heterogeneous evidence by its effect on the signed adoption decision.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Load the locked user-task assets and scorers, assign every task to a preregistered stratum h, and write the weights, utility conversion coefficients, losses, posterior thresholds, and total budget to an immutable run manifest; output the triage specification.
2. Parse the paper into load-bearing empirical claims and, for each claim-task-stratum pair, implement the smallest runnable intervention P_q plus a matched control B that differs only by that paper intervention; output a versioned check catalog rather than a completeness checklist.
3. For historical paper-task cases, replay each catalogued check and its full paired reproduction endpoint, recording paired score deltas, regressions, GPU-hours, API dollars, and adaptation hours; output the calibration table.
4. Fit and leave-one-paper-family-out calibrate the outcome likelihood indexed by check type and user-task stratum; input the calibration table and output frozen likelihood parameters plus calibration residuals.
5. Initialize the held-out paper's posterior over mu_P from the preregistered task weights and frozen likelihood, enumerate checks whose dependencies fit the remaining budget, and output the first candidate set.
6. Compute EDIV_t(q) for each candidate from expected stopping-risk reduction and measured check cost, select the largest positive value, and output the chosen check with an auditable score breakdown.
7. Execute P_q and B on the same user task, model, environment, scorer, and seed; collect their downstream outputs, score deltas, regressions, and actual costs, and output the paired observation o_q.
8. Update the posterior over mu_P with o_q, recompute false-adoption and false-rejection risk, and either return to step 6 or apply the frozen stopping rule; output adopt, reject, or inconclusive with the exact boundary crossed.
9. For evaluation only, reveal the full paired reproduction endpoint on the same weighted user-task distribution and compare its sign with the triage decision; output cost-to-correct decision, false-adoption, false-rejection, and inconclusive indicators for each locked case.
10. Repeat step 9 under a fixed check order, cheapest-first order, random EDIV order, and the proposed EDIV order while holding the check catalog and budgets identical; output the policy-level comparison that attributes any saving to adaptive selection rather than easier checks.
falsification_prediction: On the eight locked real-reuse paper-task cases, replay the saved minimal paired probe outcomes sequentially for the same agent model and environment, using each full paper-intervention-versus-control run on the user-weighted task distribution as the gold sign. If the mechanism works, median normalized cost-to-correct adoption should decrease relative to the strongest fixed-order or cheapest-first schedule while false-adoption and false-rejection rates do not increase. The single load-bearing variable is EDIV_t(q); as a negative control, randomly permute EDIV_t(q) across the still-available checks at every step while holding the check set, stop thresholds, and budget fixed. Under that intervention, the downstream cost-to-correct-adoption metric should return to the fixed-order baseline; if it does not, the claimed value-of-information selection mechanism is falsified.
compute_budget: 18 GPU-days on 80GB-class GPUs + $4,000 API for the full eight-case calibration and replay campaign, including reruns and negative controls; approximately 24 adaptation person-days are recorded as utility costs but are not compute spend.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: It generates tasks from each skill and estimates with-skill marginal utility on that artifact-conditioned suite, whereas this candidate fixes an independently specified user-task distribution, prices regressions and adoption costs, and adaptively selects paired checks to decide the sign of net benefit.

PaperBench decomposes replication into code, execution, and result-match rubric outcomes and reports a weak Code-Dev/full score correlation, whereas this candidate calibrates heterogeneous minimal checks directly against the sign of downstream user-task net utility and stops on decision risk.

AutoReproduce's sampled mini-batches and dry runs expose data-shape and executability failures inside an end-to-end reproduction pipeline, whereas this candidate chooses which paired task-level intervention check to run next by expected reduction in adoption error after costs and regressions.

SkillFoundry's execution, system, and synthetic-data tests validate contracts before a limited downstream suite, whereas this candidate treats every check as evidence about a preregistered user-distribution treatment effect and reports calibrated adopt, reject, or inconclusive decisions across held-out paper families.

what_step_was_missed: It would have needed to decouple evaluation tasks from the skill artifact, define a cost- and regression-adjusted treatment effect over the user's task distribution, and choose successive paired checks by their expected reduction in three-way adoption decision risk.
